newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas prices rise on storage buying.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas prices rise on storage buying.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for October traded mostly higher on Wednesday as players entered the market to buy supplies for sales next month, trading sources said.
Gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was talked in the C$1.30/1.32 range, up from C$1.29/1.30 last week. November gas was quoted at C$1.41/1.42, up over a dime from last week.

"It's related to terms," said a Calgary-based marketer. "People are buying gas this month for sale in November." He said prices could climb as high as C$1.37 before storage buying became unprofitable.

Export gas at Kingsgate, British Columbia was said to be trading anywhere between US$1.30 and US$1.40 per million British thermal units, as a transport restriction for maintenance on the NOVA side of the Alberta-B.C. border point neared an end, traders said.
Transport of up to 400 million cubic feet per day had been cut earlier this week. Sources said flows were expected to be back to normal late Wednesday.

Gas at Sumas, however, was discussed about 18 cents lower as injections and withdrawals were cut from the 300 MMCFD Unocal storage facility at Aitken Creek, B.C. for maintenance. The facility was expected to be back in service on October 14. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
